=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/workflow-log-analysis.yml:476-515 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The tracker-selection snippet picks the first `ai:retro` issue containing the marker instead of the most recently updated open tracker.
  WHY: With multiple open trackers, comments can be posted to a stale or obsolete issue, fragmenting the weekly-retro thread.
- scripts/workflow_retro.py:299, 316, 322 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The retryable-pattern, rate-limit detection, and wait logic are duplicated instead of reusing the shared GitHub helpers.
  WHY: Future changes to the canonical retry/backoff contract can diverge here, causing inconsistent throttling recovery on the weekly-retro path.
- tests/test_workflow_log_analysis_contract.py:74-116 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The test hardcodes 4 Semble installs and related step counts even though the weekly-retro job does not run on non-schedule triggers or when `WORKFLOW_RETRO_ENABLED` is false.
  WHY: The contract test can fail when only 3 jobs run, because the retro job is gated off outside the scheduled case.
- scripts/workflow_retro.py:747-750 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The embedded Python selector chooses the first matching tracker issue instead of preferring the active or most recently updated one.
  WHY: If duplicate `ai:retro` trackers exist, upserts can land on a stale issue rather than the intended tracker thread.
- tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py:203 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The test name still mentions only security-audit even though the body now also covers `ai:retro` skip logic.
  WHY: This is a maintainability/naming concern that obscures the broader contract the test now validates.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
